originalSourceText:
Q.9   The primary reason a SCARA robot is described as selectively compliant is that it is:

      (A) Flexible in the Z-direction and rigid in the X–Y plane

      (B) Rigid in the X–Y plane and compliant in all rotational axes

      (C) Rigid in the Z-direction while compliant in the X–Y plane

      (D) Equally compliant in all directions

       Explanation: (C) Refer Slide 4 of Lecture Manipulator Design Example

    A SCARA manipulator is designed to be rigid along the vertical (Z) axis while
       allowing limited compliance in the horizontal (X–Y) plane, making it particularly
       suitable for insertion and assembly tasks.
